newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle seen steady to up, feeders mixed.

text.p: CME live cattle futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher while feeder cattle calls ranged from 0.100 cent higher to 0.100 lower, livestock analysts said.

Active feedlot movement last week with packers still paying $68 per cwt late in the week, and the continued strong tone to cash beef, should prompt carryover support in live cattle futures. Expectations are for active retailer demand to continue for boxed beef to fill needs during May holidays, analysts said.
However, some analysts look for scale-up resistance.
The market appears overbought especially with larger fed cattle numbers seen ahead. Fund buying has incresed open interest while commercials have been hedging on the scale-up, they said.

Some analysts anticipate carryover strength in feeder cattle futures following posting of new contract highs Friday and steady corn indications. Active feedlot movement should encourage demand for replacement feeders, they said.
However, analysts cited a lower index and an overbought market. The outlook for weaker fed cattle markets ahead could reduce interest for replacement feeders, they added.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.19 to $72.13 per cwt.
